QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_16

question.text: The exchange-level open interest in 91-Day T-Bill futures is Rs. 5,000 crores. What is the applicable trading-member position limit for these futures?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 235 of the NISM Series IV workbook, the trading-member position limit for 91-Day T-Bill futures and Overnight MIBOR futures is 15% of open interest or Rs. 1,000 crore, whichever is higher. 15% of Rs. 5,000 crore = Rs. 750 crore; comparing with Rs. 1,000 crore floor: Rs. 1,000 crore is higher, so the TM limit is Rs. 1,000 crore. The Trap: Rs. 750 crore applies only the percentage and ignores the workbook's whichever-is-higher rule. Rs. 500/Rs. 600 crore reflect smaller percentages that the source does not prescribe. For GOI bond futures, the formula is different: 10% of open interest or INR 1,200 crore/INR 600 crore depending on maturity bucket per pages 234-235. Note: Per pages 234-235 and 237, position limits are linked to exchange open interest; the workbook's formula always selects whichever is higher between the percentage and the floor, not lower.
